preview: An interview experience at DE Shaw detailing the online assessment, two technical interview rounds involving DSA, Java, DBMS, System Design, and OS questions, and final selection for the internship.
content: DE Shaw Group, India Kasodariya Deep TY(I.T) – 2022-2026 Eligibility: DE Shaw was the second company to visit our campus for internships. A total of 151 students were eligible. For CS/IT Students, CGPA criteria was 7+. For other circuit branches, the criteria were 8+. Online Assessment (3rd August 2024): There was a proctored online test, which was held on Hackerrank platform. Total of 95 minutes were allotted with 25 minutes for the 1st and 35 minutes each for the 2nd and 3rd questions. Navigating between the questions was not allowed, you can go to the next question only if you submit / the time expired. Q1. Load Balancer (25 min): You are given n servers such that the ith server is active in between [ai, bi). You are also given k tasks such that tasks[i] gives the time when the current task will require a server. You have to calculate the minimum waiting time for each task to get a server of say that the task cannot be completed. Ex: servers = {{2, 3}, {5, 10}, {12, 13}, {15, 25}} tasks = {1, 7, 30, 4} answer = {1, 0, -1, 1} Explanation: For task 1 it takes one unit time to get server {2, 3}. For task 2, 7 lies in between {5, 10} so 0. For task 3 no server has time interval covering 30 hence -1. Sol: I tried the brute for approach for each task decided to iterate over the servers to see if the task can be completed and also find the minimum waiting time. The approach resulted in TLE, and I was not able to solve it in 25 minutes. (After contests realized that it was binary search.) Q2. Query Strings (35 min): Given an integer k, you start with an empty string and you can do the following two operations: 1. Append a 0 to the end of the string. 2. Append K 1s to the end of the string. Given an array of queries of size q, for each query you have to print the number of ways to form a string of length l, l+1, l+2, r where l = q[i][0], r=q[i][1]. Print the answer modulo 10e9 + 7. Ex: For k = 3, the possible strings are 0, 00, 111, 000, … Queries = {{1, 3}}, Answer = 4. Sol: I decided to follow a recursive approach, and generate all the strings of size (max of the query). Then used memorization to make it efficient. Now dp[i] contains the string of length i using the given rules. The using prefix sum we can calculate the answer efficiently. Q3. Max Sum (35 min): You are given a matrix of size 10 * 10 where the elements can be positive or negative. You are given a number n, now you need to find the sum of elements of matrix such that their indices are part of the array of size n. Ex: arr = {1, 2, 3, 6} Then we have the sum of elements as matrix [1][2] + matrix [2][3] + matrix [3][6]. In short, we have to find an arrangement of the arr to have the maximum sum of (n-1) elements. We don’t need to return the arr, just the max sum that can be formed. Sol: I can start with the first element from any row. Then I can select any number from that row, let’s say i, j. Then the row of my next element would be j. Hence, I used recursive 2d dp approach to solve the problem. dp[i][n] represent the max sum when we have to select n elements starting from ith row. For each row iterate over the whole row, see which elements give me the max sum and return that. After the OA, 12 students were selected for the interviews. TECHNICAL INTERVIEW 1: 5th August 2024 (2:30 – 3:30) The round was conducted on Hackerrank Code Pair. It had several facilities like interactive IDE, chat window, video call. The interviewers introduced themselves first and later I gave my introduction. The interviewer straight started with the DSA question. Q1. Given two vectors containing the velocity and position of the racers who are running on an infinite line. I need to tell how many overtakes were going to be performed. Sol: He pasted the question in the IDE and then gave me some time to think about it. I kept on thinking (speaking and explaining my approached at the same time). I told him that I would create a new Racer class to store the values and sort them on the basis of position. I said we can then use monotonic stack approach to solve the problem. He countered with why not sort it on the basis of velocity. I said let’s try with it, gave him the solution that would work on the basis of velocity sorting. Then he said to implement the solution, I said I am comfortable With Java as my primary language. I coded the solution, and he asked me the time complexity. Similar to: https://leetcode.com/problems/car-fleet/description/ Make sure to explain the approach well, write, if possible, on the ide while explaining. Think of edge cases. If you are unable to solve, they may give you the hint. Q2. Design a stack that would give the max element in O (1) time complexity. The question was not clear at the beginning, I asked them doubts and what exactly I needed to do. Sol: Then I realized it is similar to Min Stack but with Max element. I gave them the approach with explanation, test examples. They didn’t ask me to code it. Q3. Since I said Java is my main language, they asked me a lot of questions about Java. 1. What happens in the compilation process. 2. Does Java have garbage collector. 3. Memory Management in Java. 4. How to manually invoke the garbage collector. 5. Constructor & Destructor in Java 6. Does Java support multiple Inheritance. 7. Why it does not support? (Follow up: Nahi at ana boldo, don’t make up stuff) 8. Have you heard about thread Api in Java, and do threads communicate with each other. Then they shifted to DBMS. 1. What is normalization. 2. Explain the types. 3. Given a table containing emp_id and emp_name, another table containing emp_id, manager_id. Write a SQL query to print the table in the format, emp_name, manager_name. Think out loud and don’t be in fear. Just try to be yourself. And prepare for the worst. TECHNICAL INTERVIEW 2: 5th August 2024 (4:30 – 6:00) Only 3 students were selected for round 2. The round started where they asked me about my projects. The technologies I am familiar with. They also asked me about my certifications and why did I learn the particular tech stack. I didn’t have any knowledge about ML and since my project had ML part which was done by my team-mates, he asked me whether I was aware of what they did. He also asked me; did you face any challenge while working in teams? Q1. Give N ships and M containers the containers need to be distributed such that the maximum difference between the ships weight is minimized. Sol: I told the approach, about binary search on answer. He gave me a test case and I did a dry run to explain my approach. We ha a long discussion about the approach and he was try to convince that my answer was wrong I believe. I stayed firm and then he asked if I had to used a data structure to solve it, what I would use. I said Priority Queue of size N would also do the job. Q2. I was asked a low-level system design question to design Zomato and Swiggy or Blink-it. Sol: I started by asking about the requirements. They said I can assume and decide by myself. I asked about the items we were selling like on food or all the stuff. I started with user, name, their location (told them about the Quad Tree data structure). I also told them that I would use an Item interface for storing the items in the database. Like implementing the SOLID design principles. I also ideated over the Adapter Design Pattern. Then I said that there might be two types of users and we can use Enums to differentiate. Like the Delivery guy or Buyer. I also asked them whether the delivery system was ours or out sourcing cause then I do not need to implement delivery. They asked me where I would use which and why. Then we went to Order entity, initially I was storing userId, username, User location. I told them that I will store list of Items using Liskov’s Substitution Principle. Later, we can also store payment method. There the ma’am countered about discount. I told them that Enums can have properties and we use them to calculate discounted amount. She again countered with what about coupons and 1+1 free scheme. I said we could create a separate entity cause both of them are unrelated. Then can normalization of Orders entity, I told them the that user name was redundant and I could store just userId and retrieve the name if required. We had a long discussion over do we need user location in Order. I still said it depends on use case and scale. This could be the delivery address which might differ. If the scale is high then the storage cost might increase. I told them that the location can be updated and taken from Redis cache, that could be used at runtime to store. At last, I was asked about OS questions. 1. How do process communicate. 2. Can the process prevent from stopping itself. 3. What happens when we press Ctrl + C in a running Java program. (I said the exit code was 130 (Details Matter)). Results came out at 8:00pm and only 1 person was selected. 0.66 probability and I did it. TIPS: RELATED TO DSA: Look for patterns and keep on practicing. If you have practice good enough you will be able to do it. Try do Leet-Code 75. I have done leetcode daily questions & gfg potd for more than 8 months. I came to know about the patterns of the question because I solved similar type of questions before. RELATED TO CORE (OS, DBMS, OOPS): DBMS: https://whimsical.com/dbms-roadmap-by-love-babbar-FmUi8ffVop33t3MmpVxPCo OS: Refer to Galvin and prepare notes and revise. There is also a short pdf available online. OOPS: Do it in depth properly, in the language you do DSA. INTERVIEW TIPS: 1. Don’t live in fear, I couldn’t sleep the previous night and got so bad stomach butterflies. But I said one thing to myself it’s in my hands and I don’t want to regret it later. 2. Be Confident, and Try to give your best. (ATB)
